chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The manufacturers, when they stay awake the whole night, so it is ill-gotten gain (suh't).

key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Ill-gotten gain / usurped wealth / haram earnings

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on earnings from night-long manufacturing work in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights a specific juristic ruling where nocturnal labor by artisans renders their earnings 'suh't' (ill-gotten gain), reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing physical well-being with economic justice. This ruling underscores the principle that excessive toil compromising health or religious duties can invalidate the purity of income, a concept deeply rooted in the broader ethical framework of trade in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Malik,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The manufacturer, when he is awake the whole night, so it is an ill-gotten gain (his manfucturing)’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Shammun from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm from Misma’ ibn ‘Abd al-Malik who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a technician remains awake the whole night working, his earning becomes Suht (unlawful and filthy).’”
